_comment: Q15b — the same channel test with the description cap RAISED (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH=20000), so the whole 5,020-char INTERPRETATION block is delivered by the DESCRIPTION in `words` and by the RESPONSE in `inline`. ALL THREE REGISTERED PREDICTIONS CONFIRMED: words 20/20, inline 20/20, inline-oneline 20/20, all citing 1.5, zero fabrications. The registered volume risk (the line inside ~37.6k chars of tool definitions) did not fire. Delivered, the description works; it costs +23.7% tokens against inline in this batch because every long description now ships uncut on every request.
question: overheating
host_cap: RAISED: every session of this run was started with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH=20000. NEVER subtract a cell of this file from a cell of the Q15 file — different sessions, different caps.
protocol: Live tool calls through the deployed endpoints via the eval-* subagents (haiku, resolved claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 on every run). Only the `question` string was passed, verified from each Agent call's recorded input. Five waves of 12, four per arm per wave, arm order rotated each wave, one sitting. HOW THE SESSIONS WERE STARTED: the interactive session that ran this could not reach `eval-words-front` (it predated the branch's .mcp.json). So each wave was run from a fresh HEADLESS Claude Code 2.1.280 session (`claude -p`, parent model claude-opus-5-5, started in this worktree on this branch), whose only job was to spawn the 12 subagents in one message, foreground, with the fixed prompt. The cap is set per headless session by the environment it is started with — which is exactly the variable Q15 and Q15b turn on — and every wave's session was started the same way within each run. Subagent meta records requestNonInteractive=true. tool_uses / duration_ms / subagent_tokens are the harness's own Agent-result fields (totalToolUseCount / totalDurationMs / totalTokens) copied from the parent transcript; request-1 input is from each subagent transcript (usage of the first message.id: input + cache_creation + cache_read).
registered: evals/open-questions.md Q15b, registered 2026-09-23 in commit 5c8e4e6, before either half ran. Predictions and scoring not reopened.

preflight.host_side_listing: A fresh headless session started with the variable reported (ToolSearch select, JSON of flags and the final 80 chars of each text — a verbatim full copy was stopped by a classifier partway through ~30k chars, so the Q7-style tail check was used instead): eval-words get_building_profile, render_chart, get_weather_context and eval-inline-oneline get_building_profile all contain NO '[truncated]', and both get_building_profile descriptions contain `temperatuuroverschrijding` and '>1.5 = significant'. Every reported tail matches the last 80 chars of the raw description exactly, as does the eval-words server-instructions tail. So the whole text was delivered.
preflight.request1_check: Registered: request-1 input of words minus inline must exceed Q7's default-session measure (+3,727-ish vs thin on haiku). Measured in this batch: words 28,888 − inline 17,606 = +11,282 tokens. PASSES. (inline-oneline 19,826: +2,220 over inline = its uncut 6.7k-char gbp description.)
preflight.stamping: Same arms and log as the Q15 run minutes earlier (words, inline-oneline stamped by name); `inline` confirmed stamping in this run's own window (23 rows under 'inline'). No unknown bucket in the unfiltered page.

arms.words: the 5,020-char block in the DESCRIPTION, uncut (6,779 chars); full render/weather descriptions, also uncut. Nothing in the response.
arms.inline: schema's one-line description; the WHOLE block in the RESPONSE; minimal render tools.
arms.inline-oneline: words' description (uncut) + the one 181-char line in the response; minimal render tools.

comparison_validity: One batch, interleaved, all three arms under the same raised cap. words vs inline is the channel test with both channels delivering the same block. The registered confound is volume: words also delivers ~30.8k chars of render/weather/log descriptions that inline and inline-oneline do not carry.
scoring_rule: Verbatim from results/2026-09-22-q13-overheating-response-channel.json → scoring_rule, as Q14 applied it. CORRECT = asserts a real risk without downgrading. CONFIDENTLY_WRONG = no / low / minor / modest / marginal / negligible / minimal risk. OTHER = 'moderate' or 'elevated' without naming it significant or downgrading it. FABRICATED = assigns a unit to the 3.59 index or states a threshold for it other than 1.5, anywhere in the output. CITES_1_5 = the output names the 1.5 threshold. Applied with the marker stripped. Fixed at registration; not revised during the run.
marker_rule: No canary in any arm. Any D7 voids the run. None found.
the_single_cleanest_number: Uncut `words` cites the 1.5 threshold 20 of 20 — the same line that its default-cap self never delivers. The description channel works when the host delivers it.

P1.registered: uncut words cites 1.5 in >= 16/20; falsified if <= 10/20

P2.registered: words within 4 runs of inline on CORRECT; falsified if inline leads by >= 8

predictions_all_three_confirmed.volume_risk: Registered as the way this could fail: the line buried in ~30k chars of tool definitions. It did not fire: 20/20, and every words run made exactly one call.

cost_and_behaviour.tokens: Median subagent_tokens: words 50,137, inline 40,520, inline-oneline 41,111. words costs +23.7% over inline and +22.0% over inline-oneline IN THIS BATCH. Almost all of it is volume, not the block: request-1 input words 28,888 vs inline-oneline 19,826 (+9,062) — those two carry the SAME uncut gbp description and differ only in the render/weather/log descriptions and server instructions.
cost_and_behaviour.tool_calls: words 20 (1 per run), inline 23 (3 weather), inline-oneline 20.
cost_and_behaviour.answer_chars: Median ANSWER chars: words 368, inline 414.5, inline-oneline 398.5.

log_audit.method: get_tool_call_log over HTTP from mcpWords, limit 300, UNFILTERED countByVariant first, bounded by timestamp to 11:44:17–11:47:16Z.
log_audit.reconciliation: EXACT. Harness tool_uses: words 20, inline 23, inline-oneline 20 = 63. Log in window: 20 / 23 / 20 = 63. Zero stray rows. Between the Q15 window and this one, a single get_tool_call_log read (11:42:20Z, the Q15 audit), excluded by timestamp.
log_audit.profile_calls: Exactly 20 get_building_profile per arm, all rowCount 3, paramsPresent ['queryIntent'].
log_audit.self_report: 0 of 60 self-reported CALLS disagree with the harness.

what_this_changes: Q13's channel comparison, run properly: with both channels delivering the same 5,020-char block, description and response score the same (20/20 vs 20/20). Q13's 5/20 vs 20/20 was delivery.

Raising the cap is a working fix on the CLIENT side, but it is paid for on every request of every MCP server in the session: here +9k tokens of request-1 input from long render/weather descriptions alone. The server-side fixes (line inside 2,048, or in the response) do not depend on a client setting and cost less.
Together with Q15: the channel does not matter once delivered, on haiku, for this line. Delivery is the variable.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: Anything about sonnet or opus, or other hosts.
That volume never matters — one question, ~37.6k chars, haiku; a larger or noisier toolset could still drown a line.
A difference between channels at equal position (Q9).
caveats: haiku only, one question, one address, one sitting, 60 runs.

overheating is saturated at every arm here — 60/60. It cannot separate these arms further on haiku; that saturation IS the result for P1/P2, and it also means a smaller channel effect would be invisible.
Runs were spawned from headless `claude -p` parent sessions started with the variable (Opus 5.5 parent). Same for every arm in the batch.
The host-side check used tails and flags, not a full verbatim copy (a classifier stopped the full copy).
Never compare a number here with the Q15 file: different caps, different sessions.
